chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem if a man gives to another man on behalf of two heads, and three, and four, meaning the Fitra.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitra, the obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can one person pay Fitra for multiple family members?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in fulfilling the Fitra obligation, permitting a single payer to discharge the duty for multiple dependents by providing one share per person. It reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that the obligation is tied to the individual's capacity and household structure, allowing for efficient distribution of charity during Eid al-Fitr. The ruling underscores the communal aspect of Zakat, where the head of the household often acts as the representative for his family members.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem if a man gives to another man on behalf of two heads, and three, and four, meaning the Fitra’.
en.sarwar: 17. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of our people from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not harmful to pay al-Fitrah for two, three, or four people to one man.’”
